rationale.paradigm_idiomaticity: Recursion over lists with accumulators (fill_rows/6, row_step/6, trace/11) and head pattern matching on the state (trace(m,...), trace(x,...), trace(y,...)) is in the logic style, and the final pair of atom_chars/2 calls is fine. Cuts in start_state/5 are acceptable. However, the if-then-else chains with =:= inside trace/11 and the max/2 expression chains are functional/imperative DP rather than relational. start_state/5 uses cuts to emulate if-else (red-ish). A 5 would need a cleaner use of clause indexing or a helper that picks the predecessor state, with less deterministic-cut flavor.
rationale.language_idiomaticity: It uses library(assoc), atom_chars/2, last/2 and is with max, and the module header is correct. Weak points: neg_inf/1 is a predicate used as a constant, there is a dead and odd p(_,_,GO,GE) re-construction in row0_ recursion (passes p(_,_,GO,GE) with fresh singletons rather than the P argument), and a stray `</br>` at the end of the file is a syntax-level defect. rows_pairs builds a huge assoc keyed by I-J when the rows could be indexed with nth0 or the tables stored as arrays. A 5 requires removing these oddities and using the library more simply.
rationale.readability: The header comment explains the c(M,X,Y) states and the transitions. The trace/11 comment documents the arguments. Names such as fill_row, row_step, start_state are clear. But trace/11 has 11 arguments, nested if-then-else, short names (Mu, Xu, Ml, Yl, Md), and row_step uses a sliding window [PD,PU|PRest] which is subtle. The row0_ clause is confusing because of the re-built p/4 term. More comments on the traceback logic and fewer parameters (bundling the table and parameters) would earn a 5.
rationale.design: The solution separates DP fill, table conversion and traceback, and shares fill/4 between score and align. Parameters are bundled in p/4. Drawbacks: the traceback re-derives predecessor states by recomputing scores instead of storing pointers, trace/11 threads too many arguments, the table is stored twice (list of rows and an assoc of all cells), which costs memory and is O(log n) lookups, and the same transition formulas are duplicated between fill and trace. alignment_score computes the whole table instead of two rows. A 5 would use a single table representation and a smaller traceback signature.

anti_patterns: cuts in start_state/5 emulating if-else instead of clause conditions
nested if-then-else chains with =:= for traceback decisions
redundant conversion of row lists into a large assoc
neg_inf/1 predicate used as a constant
stray </br> text at the end of the file
justification: The solution uses accumulator recursion, clause-head dispatch on the DP state and library(assoc), so it is broadly reasonable Prolog. It is let down by the arithmetic-heavy if-then-else traceback in trace/11, cuts in start_state/5, the redundant list-of-rows plus assoc representation, and sloppy details like the re-built p/4 in row0_ and the stray `</br>` line. The decomposition into fill, table access and traceback is sensible but the traceback signature is heavy and formulas are duplicated.
